notes_markdown:
**Heads-up before you update:** RAW photos now open with **Denoise at 0**.
RAWs you developed earlier that relied on the automatic noise reduction
render without it until you turn Denoise up (see Changed). And a series
aligned with this version keeps its landmark points in a new form: an
older culler reading it may place points on server photos you saved with
`J` in the wrong spot (see Fixed).

### New

- **RAW photos open in the camera's look.** Opening the develop panel
  on a RAW the camera shot in Vivid now shows it in that look, matched
  to its JPEG's exposure, instead of a dark, flat render — and the
  camera JPEG stays up until the look is ready, so the switch barely
  shows. It's a starting point, not an edit: the sliders sit at 0, the
  photo isn't marked edited, nothing is saved until you change
  something, and Reset returns to the look. Choose **Neutral** in the
  look picker to start flat. Photos you've already developed keep their
  picture. Cameras culler has no look for open flat, as before.
- **Finished jobs report in the top-right corner.** When an upload, a
  batch, **Save edits** or a `J` finishes, its result appears as a
  notice where the progress pill just was — what happened, to how many
  photos and where, the photos that failed and why, and a button such as
  **Open album** or **Retry in Batch…**. A notice you didn't look at
  waits behind a bell, and `Shift+N` (or a click on the bell) lists
  everything from the last two weeks. The status line at the bottom
  keeps what you did yourself; errors show in both places. Three
  ongoing server problems also leave one notice when they start — a
  scan that lost pages (with **Rescan**), ratings and flags that stop
  syncing, and edit history the server stops accepting — and none
  repeats while the problem lasts.
- **Select photos with the mouse alone.** Hover a thumbnail in the
  filmstrip or the Grid and an empty box appears in its corner — click
  it to select the photo, click a selected photo's check to deselect it,
  `Shift`+click the box to select a run. The cursor follows the click,
  so `P`, `X` or a rating then marks the whole set you just ticked. A
  click anywhere else on the thumbnail still only moves the cursor, and
  the box fades when the mouse rests, so it never gets in the way of the
  keyboard.
- **Grid, Survey and Compare have buttons.** Each view now has a bar
  along the top with its actions as buttons that show their keys —
  Peek, Size, Group, Batch and Done in the Grid; Winnow, Keep one,
  Dismiss, Next moment and Done in Survey; Pick, Reject, Pane, Promote,
  Swap and Exit in Compare — so you can work every view start to finish
  with the mouse. The ungrouped Grid gets a box that selects all its
  photos, a peek gets a **Back** button on the rail, the `⋯` menu gets
  **Undo** and **Redo**, and crop gets a **Cancel** button.
- **Drag photos onto folders and albums.** With the Sources panel kept
  open, drag a thumbnail from the filmstrip or the Grid — or the whole
  selection, by dragging one of its photos — onto a folder of the open
  folder to move it there, onto another folder source to copy it, or onto
  an album of the open server to add it; in sort mode, onto a numbered
  cell. A label beside the pointer says what letting go will do (or why
  it won't), `⌥` flips move and copy, `Esc` cancels, and holding over a
  closed folder opens it. Moved photos stay in view at their new place.
- **More places to drag to and from.** The photo in the main view drags
  too (at fit zoom). Drop on **+ New folder** or **+ New album**, type a
  name, and the photos go straight into it. Drop a folder's photos on a
  server or one of its albums — or a server's photos on a folder — and
  the batch panel opens with the upload or download filled in for just
  those photos, waiting for you to press the button. And a folder
  dragged in from Finder opens, like `O`.
- **Reorder saved filters and sort folders by dragging.** Every row in
  the `Cmd/Ctrl+F` list and in the Sort destinations card now has a grip;
  drag it up or down and the other rows make room, the number keys
  renumbering as you go so you can see what each digit will do before
  you let go. Letting go saves the new order and the status line names
  the new number ("Portraits is now on 2"); `Esc`, or letting go away
  from the card, puts everything back.

### Changed

- **Landmark points are part of a photo's undo history.** Each step now
  holds a photo's frame *and* its alignment points, so `Cmd/Ctrl+Z` on an
  aligned photo takes both back in one step, `Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z` puts them
  back, and a history-row click or a snapshot restores them too. A
  series reference whose points changed gets its own *Landmarks · N
  points* step, and undoing it says how many aligned photos keep their
  crops (undo stays per photo). Steps saved by earlier versions leave the
  points as they are.
- **Applying a series twice keeps both steps.** A second Done on the
  same photo is its own history step, so the first alignment stays a
  point you can go back to.
- After **Discard edits** on a server photo, `Cmd+Z` now brings the
  alignment points back along with the grade and the crop.
- **Sorting into a folder inside the one you have open keeps the photos
  in view.** A sort-mode Move into one of its subfolders (or its top
  level) no longer makes the photos vanish until a rescan: they stay
  where you were looking, now living in their new folder, and the folder
  counts in the sources pane move at once. A folder view they left drops
  them; the folder they went to shows them.
- **RAW denoise now starts off.** The automatic, ISO-scaled noise
  reduction softened fine detail, so a RAW now opens with Denoise at 0;
  turn it up on the photos that need it (the row's hover suggests a
  strength for the photo's ISO). RAWs you developed before this release
  that relied on the automatic strength now render without it. Opening
  a RAW in the develop pane is also quicker, since the smoothing pass no
  longer runs by default.
=======
- **`Esc` closes the help overlay first**, like every other floating
  panel: with help open, `Esc` closes it and does nothing else — it no
  longer also leaves crop, a series, the Grid or the sources pane, and
  inside a stack or a pivot it now closes help instead of doing nothing.
  The next `Esc` does what it always did.
- **Editing never changes the camera.** In a tethered session, `[` / `]`
  (manual focus) and the info panel's exposure − / + buttons now switch
  off with the develop pane open, in crop, and in Compare, Survey and
  Match series — as the remote shutter already did. The camera's
  settings still show; the controls come back when you return to the
  photos.

### Fixed

- **Blown highlights in a RAW no longer turn black.** A burnt-out window
  or sky could render as a solid black patch with a bright fringe while
  developing a RAW (and in a JPEG made from it at reduced size); it now
  stays white, as in the camera's JPEG.

- `Esc` with the `⋯` menu open inside a stack, the Grid or Survey now
  closes just the menu instead of also leaving where you are, and
  choosing Compare, Survey or Match series from the `⋯` menu while in
  the Grid now leaves the Grid first, the way their keys do.
- **The quarter turn is undoable.** `R` / `Shift+R` outside crop mode
  now records a *Rotate right* / *Rotate left* step — it used to leave
  no step at all.
- **Undo after `Shift+J` no longer crops twice.** Overwriting the JPEG
  records an *Overwrote JPEG* step and undo stops there, saying the
  earlier states belong to the `.orig` backup — before, stepping past it
  re-applied an old crop to the already-cropped JPEG.
- **Landmark points stay on the features you clicked** on server photos
  culler has saved with `J` before. A point placed while the pane showed
  culler's cropped render used to land in the wrong spot once the RAW
  appeared or after the next `J`; now it stays put on both, a series
  re-aligns after a re-render instead of refusing, and the Match series
  crop frame on such a reference is right too. Points an earlier version
  placed on a render are moved over by themselves when culler can prove
  where they belong, and the walk asks you to check them when it can't.
  Note: an older version of culler reading a series saved by this one
  may place points on these photos in the wrong spot.
- Counts of one read "1 photo", not "1 photos", on buttons, receipts,
  status lines and the batch panel.
